sentences.text: Heard on the question of admission.
Since the appeal involves arguable point, therefore, it is admitted for final hearing.
Also heard on I.A. No.6051/2025, which is the first application filed under Section 389(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 on behalf of appellant for suspension of sentence and grant of bail.

Vide the impugned judgment dated 06.03.2025 passed by the Court of Tenth Additional Sessions Judge and Special Judge (OAW), District Bhopal, in ST No.842/2019, the appellant has been convicted under Sections 376 and 342 of the Indian Penal Code and sentenced thereunder to suffer RI for 10 years and 01 year respectively with fine of Rs.5000/- and Rs.500/-
respectively, with default stipulations.
Learned counsel for the appellant has submitted that from the case of prosecution and story narrated by the prosecutrix, it can be easily make out that it is a false case.

entities.text: Court of Tenth Additional Sessions Judge and Special Judge (OAW), District Bhopal
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: He has further submitted that the prosecutrix was a tenant of the present appellant and since the appellant wanted to vacate the premises rented out to the prosecutrix, therefore, to avoid the said action, she 2 CRA-2694-2025 made a false complaint against the appellant.

He has further submitted that the prosecutrix, in her statement, had stated that before committing rape, the appellant caused injuries upon her and even bit on her neck, but the doctor in its report has very categorically stated that no injuries were found over the body of the prosecutrix.

He has also contended that the alleged incident was said to have been committed at a market place that too at about 11.30 pm, but report whereof was made after two Vishal Singh Tomar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190248965/
1 days of the alleged incident and no sufficient explanation for reporting the matter to the police belatedly was given.

entities.text: Vishal Singh Tomar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He has submitted that considering the whole scenario, it can be said that the appellant has been falsely implicated.

He has also submitted that even the trial Court failed to appreciate the defence taken by the appellant properly and as such, it is prayed that suspending the sentence awarded to the appellant, he may be enlarged on bail.

On the other hand, learned Government Advocate has opposed the prayer of bail and submitted that looking to the nature of offence committed by the appellant, he is not entitled to be enlarged on bail.

Considering the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of record,
prima facie, I find substance in the submissions advanced by learned counsel for the appellant.
Thus, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, I.A. No.6051/2025 is allowed.

Accordingly, it is directed that the remaining jail sentence awarded to appellant shall remain suspended and he be released on bail subject to his depositing the amount of fine, if not already deposited, and on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- with a surety bond of like amount 3 CRA-2694-2025 to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for his appearance before the Registry of this Court on 01.07.2025 and on such other dates as may be fixed in this regard.
I.A. No.6051/2025 is, therefore, allowed and disposed of.
